content:
sylvia: quick sanity check request — running a fresh H100 vs L40S SKU sweep and seeing a weird p99 blowup on L40S for longctx + continuous batching. can someone eyeball the numbers?

ravi: pinging you. which model / seq / batch?

sylvia: model=mosaicml/7b-v0, seq=4096, batch=8, batching=continuous, kvcache=on. single-machine runs. summary: H100 p95 ~42ms p99 ~210ms; L40S p95 ~60ms p99 ~850ms. (these felt off)

alex: ouch. can you paste the exact run command + driver/kernel versions? also are these on dedicated nodes or our dev pool?

sylvia: running from our perf harness: 
```
./run_bench --model mosaicml/7b-v0 --seq 4096 --batch 8 --mode continuous --kv-cache --kernel=auto --devices 1
```
NVIDIA driver 535.54, CUDA 12.2. L40S was in dev-pool-zone-b, H100 on perf-ded-1.

kevin: first suspicion: kernel selection / fallback + power/thermal. L40S bandwidth and L2 differ vs H100 and runtime sometimes picks a fallback kernel for long sequences. are you running fp16 or any quant?

sylvia: fp16, no quant. verified env matches.

perf-bot: note: attached baseline curves for mosaicml/7b-v0 (2025-10-12). link: https://perf.internal/redwood/curves/7b-v0-20251012

ravi: can you run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` in parallel or `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw,clocks.current.sm,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1` during the run? DVFS/power limit differences can explain p99 spikes. also check kernel selection logs (/tmp/redwood/kernel_select.log).

sylvia: running now on L40S with monitoring. i also grabbed /tmp/redwood/kernel_select.log — here's the interesting fragment: 
```
[LOG] model=mosaicml/7b-v0 seq=4096 batch=8 devices=1
[LOG] kernel selected: attn_fallback_longseq (cost_est=1.2) 
[LOG] reason: memory_layout_mismatch -> fallback
```

alex: there we go — fallback kernel. attn_fallback_longseq is known to be slower for long sequences on L40S (single-threaded path occasionally). try forcing a different kernel selector: `--kernel=prefer_fast` or `--kernel=prefer_parallel` to see if runtime picks the optimized aten kernels. also sanity-run with `--batch=4` to see scaling.

kevin: also run with `nvidia-smi -pm 1` + `nvidia-smi -pl <value>` to lock power, or compare with H100's power-limit. thermal throttling can make kernels behave like fallback triggers due to clock drops.

sylvia: ok re-ran with `--kernel=prefer_fast` and set power limit to 250W on L40S (dev-pool allows that). new numbers: L40S p95 46ms p99 210ms. looks similar to H100 now. I think kernel selection + power headroom were the culprits.

ravi: nice. so actionable items: 1) add a quick-check in perf harness to log chosen kernel and warn if fallback selected for longctx; 2) add an optional power-lock step in our dev-pool bench job; 3) create a ticket to make kernel selection deterministic for the longctx path.

sylvia: filing ticket now: PR/issue references: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 (bench harness change) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/2189 (kernel selection follow-up). added repro notes and the kernel_select.log snippet.

perf-bot: :thumbsup: automated: attached CI benchmark run (L40S forced kernel) -> passes baseline checks.

kevin: thanks for digging in. we should also add a short note in the SKU docs about L40S longctx caveat until runtime change lands.

sylvia: will add to docs. closing the loop here — thanks everyone for the quick triage.
